messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for /streaming/generate on dedicated-pool 'pool-7'. p99=5.4s (SLO=2.5s) over 5m window. queue_depth=320, inflight=410. paging #incidents. :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): acked. I'm on it. tagging infra + runtime.

ajay (infra): looking. can someone paste current pool topology and the autoscaler state?

henry (sre): grafana link -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/pool-7 - p95=1.2s p99=5.4s; 1m spike at 17:22 UTC. warmup_rate=0.8 nodes/min, autoscaler state=scale_up_pending (handshake_wait).

leah (runtime): seeing a lot of "handshake_timeout" in pool-7 logs, and cold KV cache fills on new nodes. warmup tasks are timing out at ~45s. root cause likely coldstart + kernel compilation spikes on new GPU types.

devon (support): customer-observed symptom: streaming stalls where clients get partial data then stall until timeout. getting 15 tickets so far, two customers reporting 30s+ stalls.

maria (oncall): impact: degraded streaming for dedicated customers on pool-7; some timeouts. escalate to SEs + acct. Ajay, can you attempt a manual add of 2 warm nodes?

ajay (infra): running manual scale now. Command:

```
redwoodctl dedicated scale --pool pool-7 --add 2 --type gtx-rtx --reason "incident 1798765432"
```

ajay (infra): autoscaler accepted request but new nodes are pending handshake. cluster events show driver module loading delays on those hosts. ETA for warmup ~2-4m after handshake completes.

leah (runtime): to speed warmup I'm triggering pre-warm init on the nodes that joined. running warmup script and prepopulating KV.

```
#!/bin/bash
for host in ${NEW_HOSTS}; do
  ssh $host 'systemctl start redwood-runtime && /opt/redwood/bin/prewarm --model llama-13b --kv --load-weights'
done
```

henry (sre): quick metric snapshot after adding 2 nodes: queue_depth -> 210, p99 -> 4.1s. improvement but still above SLO. tail latencies remain; streaming stalls persist intermittently.

leah (runtime): observed that a subset of requests triggers long tail because they hit cold attention-kernel paths + large sequence lengths. lowering max_batch_size on pool-7 might reduce per-request worst-case latency. Propose: reduce batch from 64->32 and enable prefix caching for streaming endpoints.

maria (oncall): do it. Also, can we route small/interactive customers to hosted fallback model (latency-optimized) while pool recovers? Need to protect SLOs.

ajay (infra): creating a temporary routing rule to send 20% of traffic to fallback-hosted (opt-lite) and 80% remain on dedicated. Patch:

```
redwoodctl routing update --route /streaming/generate --add-backend fallback-hosted:opt-lite:0.2 --apply
```

henry (sre): after routing change: p99 -> 3.1s, queue_depth -> 120, streaming error-rate down ~45%. still sporadic stalls correlated with large sequence length requests.

devon (support): drafted customer-facing note: "We're investigating increased streaming latency impacting dedicated customers on pool-7. We've rerouted some traffic to a latency-optimized fallback and are scaling pool capacity. ETA for full recovery 30-60m. We'll post updates every 15m." Want me to send?

maria (oncall): yes, send. mention affected region NA-west and that no data loss is expected. add contact link to SEs. :white_check_mark:

devon (support): posted to customers and to #customers-ops.

leah (runtime): follow-up: found autoscaler handshake backlog due to our healthcheck threshold of 3s for init probe. New nodes failing healthcheck while background JIT triggers. Lowering healthcheck threshold to 10s for warmup path to allow nodes to register then mark them healthy after prewarm succeeded. Will roll config to pool-7 only.

```
redwoodctl pools update pool-7 --healthcheck-init-timeout 10s
```

ajay (infra): applied change. note: this increases window where partially-initialized nodes may accept work; we'll route lower weight to them until fully warmed.

henry (sre): verification: new nodes are now passing registration; warmup completed on 3 nodes. p99 trending down to 2.6s. streaming stalls mostly resolved for small sequences. Large seq tail remains for ~0.5% of requests.

maria (oncall): good. schedule manual mitigation: 1) keep fallback routing at 20% for 30m, 2) maintain reduced batch size, 3) prewarm further for predicted burst windows.

leah (runtime): additional mitigation: enable KV-prefetch for streaming clients that set 'expected_length' header. Quick patch applied to edge router to use header hint.

henry (sre): monitoring shows p95=1.1s p99=2.6s, error-rate back to baseline. queue_depth=30. Good stabilization.

maria (oncall): handing off to next oncall in 45m. please continue monitoring and start a postmortem doc. Note suspected root causes: (1) rapid burst exceeded autoscaler handshake capacity, (2) coldstart JIT/kernel compile delays, (3) aggressive init healthcheck aborted early.

devon (support): capturing customer impact numbers: 23 support tickets, 4 escalations, customers A,B,C affected intermittently. will attach logs and client traces to the incident doc.

maria (oncall): thanks. next steps: create incident page, assign owners: infra (ajay) to rework warmup runbook, runtime (leah) to add safer healthcheck/warmup config, SRE (henry) to tune routing and fallback policies. I'll run the postmortem tomorrow. :memo:

incident-bot: Incident update logged: incident_id=INC-1798765432, severity=sev2, duration=~42m, pages=3. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-1798765432

maria (oncall): closing thread here. continuing async in the incident doc. thanks everyone for fast responses. :pray:
